title: introduce-batch-orchestration-cost-telemetry-profiles
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: Many tenants run with generic batching/cache/quant defaults that either miss cost savings or breach latency SLOs depending on workload shape. This PR adds a lightweight "cost telemetry profile" pipeline that synthesizes per-tenant (and per-model) batch/cache/quant recommendations from observed token-length distributions, cold-start rates, and KV-cache hit patterns. The goal is automated, safe defaults that reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs and providing conservative fallbacks.
detailed_description: This change introduces: 1) a telemetry-driven profile generator (ct-profilegen) that consumes sampling metrics and emits a ranked set of candidate profiles (batch size, batch timeout, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile_id) with confidence scores; 2) a small runtime hook in the batch orchestrator to accept a profile priority list and apply the highest-confidence compatible profile at request routing time; 3) a compact on-disk catalog format (pkg/telemetry/cost_profiles.yaml) and migration/backfill tooling to propose profiles for existing tenants; 4) Console integration: a profile suggestions card (Console) with Explain mode showing expected cost delta and latency impact; 5) safety controls: feature-flagged rollout, canary assignment by tenant cohort, and automatic rollback if 95th-pct latency regresses beyond configured budget. Backfill is opt-in: ct-profilegen backfill --tenant <id> returns a dry run. Benchmarks: end-to-end simulation on sampled traffic shows 8-14% token-unit cost reduction for medium-tail workloads and no measurable p95 latency regression under our test harness. The PR includes unit tests for the scoring heuristics, e2e backfill dry-run tests, and a small perf harness used for the numbers above.

release_notes:
- Add telemetry-driven cost profile generator (ct-profilegen) to propose batching/cache/quant defaults per tenant.
- Console: profile suggestion card with explain mode and estimated cost/latency delta.
- Runtime: orchestrator respects profile priority lists and falls back to safe defaults.
- Migration: opt-in backfill CLI and catalog format.
- Safety: feature flag, canary rollout, and automatic rollback on latency regressions.
how_to_verify: Run: cli/ct-profilegen --sample-source=metrics-db --dry-run --tenant=<id> to get suggested profiles
Deploy feature-flagged orchestrator and assign a small tenant cohort for canary
Validate Console shows expected delta in the Suggestion card and clicking Explain shows scoring breakdown
Run tests: make test-unit && make test-e2e(cost-profile-backfill)
notes_for_operators: The cost_profiles.yaml includes compatibility matrix entries. If you observe unexpected latency spikes after applying a profile, use the 'profile revert' endpoint or disable the feature flag. Backfill uses historical sampling and will not autopromote profiles without manual approval unless the tenant is part of the auto-apply cohort defined in charts/values-ctprofiles.yaml.
internal_metrics_expected: unit_cost_delta_pct: -8 to -14 for medium-tail workloads; p95_latency_delta_ms: ~0 (safety budget 5%); kv_cache_hit_increase_pct: 2-6
changelog_summary: Introduce cost-telemetry profiles: generation CLI, orchestrator integration, Console suggestions, backfill tooling, and safety rollouts; improves unit economics with minimal latency risk.
